section_summary: This section records Japanese budget debates from late 1933 through 1934, especially the tension between military spending, agricultural relief, taxation and borrowing. It includes file notes, embassy reporting, extracts from financial reports, the published 1934–35 budget, and a lengthy memorandum assessing whether Japan could continue financing its deficits through bond sales.

subfiles.title: Japanese military spending and budget pressures
subfiles.about: Grew discusses debt-financed military spending, inflation fears and claims that farm relief was sacrificed.
subfiles.summary: The despatch warns that munitions spending has created prosperity through borrowing while the national debt grows sharply. It describes Takahashi's effort to restrain expenditure and quotes an army rebuttal to criticism of military appropriations.

subfiles.title: Comment on military statements and farmers
subfiles.doc_type: Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum fragment
subfiles.about: The note assesses press reaction to army and navy claims about agitation among farmers.
subfiles.summary: Military statements reportedly intensified criticism; Araki may support supplementary agricultural relief.

subfiles.title: Comment on Admiral Suetsugu's interview
subfiles.doc_type: Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum fragment
subfiles.about: The writer evaluates the plausibility of statements attributed to Suetsugu.
subfiles.summary: The writer considers Suetsugu's reported remarks indiscreet but plausible.

subfiles.title: The Army's Solicitude for the Welfare of the Japanese Farmers
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, United States Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The despatch addresses the army's response to farmers' dissatisfaction with budget allocations.
subfiles.summary: The summary reports that large military appropriations and limited agricultural relief threatened relations between farmers and the armed services. Army and navy press statements apparently harmed their cause, while Araki began advocating assistance.

subfiles.title: Japanese government secret funds
subfiles.about: The memorandum compares current secret-fund appropriations with earlier Japanese allocations.
subfiles.summary: It reports a sharp rise in unaccounted government funds to roughly 14 million yen.

subfiles.title: The Army's Solicitude for the Welfare of the Japanese Farmers, continuation
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, United States Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The despatch quotes the army's defense of its budget and describes Araki's support for farm relief.
subfiles.summary: The army alleges that critics are trying to estrange civilians from the military. Araki subsequently urges cabinet ministers to approve agricultural rehabilitation, though the finance minister opposes increasing expenditure.

subfiles.title: Foreign-loan negotiations and Tokyo Electric Light bonds
subfiles.about: The note cites a report that Tokyo Electric Light intended to alter its foreign-currency bond coupons.
subfiles.summary: It records a proposed cancellation of dollar and pound payment at former gold parity.

subfiles.title: Budget for 1934–35
subfiles.about: The note points to Grew's report on cabinet approval of the 1934–35 budget.
subfiles.summary: It cross-references a despatch detailing appropriations approved on December 2.

subfiles.title: Budget appropriations and Rice Control Act
subfiles.about: The extract lists ordinary and extraordinary appropriations and discusses rice-price controls.
subfiles.summary: It gives departmental spending totals and notes that the Rice Control Act's main test would come with the seasonal price decline.

subfiles.title: Miscellaneous Financial Notes
subfiles.about: The extract describes improving Japanese banking and industrial results.
subfiles.summary: It cites higher rayon output, dividends and employee bonuses as signs of recovery.

subfiles.title: The Thirty-Third Financial and Economic Annual of Japan (1933)
subfiles.about: The sheet identifies and records the filing of a Japanese finance annual.
subfiles.summary: Two copies of the 1933 annual were filed in overflow.

subfiles.title: Instruction for a report on foreign trade
subfiles.about: The referenced telegram requests a report on trade and Japan's capital resources.
subfiles.summary: It requests analysis of three years of foreign trade and its effect on capital resources.

subfiles.title: Gold purchasing law of Japan
subfiles.about: The note points to a report on a gold-purchasing bill introduced in the Diet.
subfiles.summary: It cross-references an outline of the bill's provisions.

subfiles.title: Unidentified financial table fragment
subfiles.about: Only scattered figures survive in the OCR.
subfiles.summary: The figures are insufficient to identify the table's subject.

subfiles.title: Financial trends report extract
subfiles.about: The extract discusses the proposed 1935–36 budget and Takahashi's appointment as finance minister.
subfiles.summary: A newspaper estimate puts the budget at 2.21 billion yen, with military appropriations exceeding one billion yen. Financial circles reportedly welcomed Takahashi's return.

subfiles.title: Illegible approval and distribution slip
subfiles.about: The page appears to contain approval and distribution markings.
subfiles.summary: The OCR does not preserve a readable substantive note.

subfiles.title: Comment on items in the 1934–35 budget
subfiles.doc_type: Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum fragment
subfiles.about: The note highlights foreign-service, Manchurian and army equipment appropriations.
subfiles.summary: It points to funds for Japanese residents abroad, Manchuria, foreign-service allowances and new arms.

subfiles.title: Budget for 1934–35
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, United States Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The embassy transmits the principal headings of Japan's enacted general budget for fiscal 1934–35.
subfiles.summary: The transcript reproduces the March 20 proclamation and fixes general revenue and expenditure at 2,112,133,483 yen. It details ordinary and extraordinary accounts, including borrowing, debt-related receipts, military spending, public works, education, agricultural rehabilitation and colonial expenditures. The budget provides a detailed basis for assessing Japan's reliance on loans and its allocation of funds across departments.

subfiles.title: Budget approval and gold purchases bill
subfiles.about: The note references budget approval, a gold purchases bill and revised fiscal estimates.
subfiles.summary: It points to a despatch on Diet action and expected revenue and expenditure changes.

subfiles.title: Reduction in estimated budget deficit
subfiles.about: The extract attributes a lower deficit to revenue growth and expenditure cuts.
subfiles.summary: It reports an estimated 140 million yen reduction in the deficit.

subfiles.title: Foreign press reports on Japanese debt
subfiles.about: The extract summarizes European newspaper reports on Japanese borrowing and public debt.
subfiles.summary: It cites a planned Manchurian deficit loan and an estimate of 7.814 billion yen in public debt.

subfiles.title: Japanese currency policy
subfiles.about: The note references a financial report containing an article on yen devaluation.
subfiles.summary: It points to statements in Keizai on devaluation and currency policy.

subfiles.title: Navy plans for its 1935–36 budget
subfiles.about: The note references navy planning independent of the political situation.
subfiles.summary: The Navy Department reportedly intended to set its budget according to its requirements.

subfiles.title: 1935–36 budget, indebtedness and bonds
subfiles.about: The note references cabinet budget plans and government borrowing.
subfiles.summary: It points to discussion of the 1935–36 budget, national debt and bonds.

subfiles.title: Military demands and national indebtedness
subfiles.about: The extract describes anticipated army and navy demands and gives a debt estimate.
subfiles.summary: Newspapers question budget discipline as the navy seeks a much larger appropriation and the army plans aviation expansion. A June estimate places government indebtedness at about 8.83 billion yen.

subfiles.title: Estimated naval appropriation for 1935–36
subfiles.about: The note references a navy estimate exceeding 700 million yen.
subfiles.summary: It questions whether the finance minister can reduce the navy's demand.

subfiles.title: Estimated balance of payments of Japan during 1933
subfiles.from: T. Yumoto, citing Ministry of Finance figures
subfiles.about: The table estimates Japanese merchandise, gold and invisible-trade payments for 1933.
subfiles.summary: It gives credits, debits and balances for principal balance-of-payments categories.

subfiles.title: Government finance under Minister Fujii
subfiles.about: The extract discusses Fujii's military-budget and farm-relief pressures.
subfiles.summary: It reports proposed cuts to ministry requests while warning that further deficits and export restrictions could threaten the yen.

subfiles.title: Government finance, bonds and Osaka disaster
subfiles.about: The extract considers budget demands, bond absorption, tax policy and the Osaka disaster.
subfiles.summary: Military spending, farm relief and damage from the September typhoon increase pressure on the budget. Officials argue banks can absorb more deficit bonds, while other observers warn that issuance may be nearing its limit. The government considers taxation but resists abrupt policy changes.

subfiles.title: Estimates for the 1935–36 budget
subfiles.about: The note references a report on government finance and budget estimates.
subfiles.summary: It points to estimates for the 1935–36 fiscal year.

subfiles.title: Proposed taxes and 1935–36 budget allocations
subfiles.about: The extract reports proposed tax increases and preliminary ministry allocations.
subfiles.summary: The finance minister prepares a modest tax increase, while the ministry's initial 1935–36 budget estimate cuts most extraordinary requests.

subfiles.title: Budget and financial trends for 1935–36
subfiles.about: The note references a report on the budget and reaction to Takahashi's appointment.
subfiles.summary: It cites press budget figures and improved financial confidence after Takahashi's return.

subfiles.title: The budget for 1935–36 and financial trends
subfiles.about: The extract reports the cabinet's budget estimate and financial reaction to Takahashi.
subfiles.summary: The cabinet's proposed 2.21 billion yen budget includes over one billion yen for army and navy spending. Financial circles reportedly welcome Takahashi as finance minister.

subfiles.title: Press comment on Japanese spending in Manchukuo
subfiles.about: British press comment addresses Japanese military expenditure in Manchukuo and the yen.
subfiles.summary: Takahashi reportedly urges reduced army expenditure in Manchukuo. Press commentary links yen depreciation, raw-material import costs, overseas spending and the next budget deficit to a worsening exchange position.

subfiles.title: Assessment of claims that Japan is nearing financial exhaustion
subfiles.doc_type: Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum, concluding pages
subfiles.about: The memorandum weighs predictions of Japanese financial collapse against officers' assessments.
subfiles.summary: Experienced officers in Japan and China report no immediate signs that Japan is financially close to collapse. The writer argues that predictions require detailed evidence and must account for political commitment as well as financial statistics. It introduces attached analyses by Feis, Stinebower and Sturgeon that likewise find insufficient evidence of an imminent crisis.

subfiles.title: Japanese Fiscal Position
subfiles.about: The memorandum analyzes Japanese deficits, debt, banking capacity, bond yields, gold holdings and economic indicators.
subfiles.summary: The analysis explains the limits of Japan's published general-account figures and traces rising deficits, military expenditure and public debt. It finds that banks and the National Deposits Bureau hold large amounts of government bonds, yet compares their portfolios with United States banks and sees room for further absorption. Bank of Japan holdings, bond yields and production indices likewise show no clear immediate financing crisis. The memorandum identifies uncertainty about Japan's total gold and foreign-exchange reserves while asking whether borrowing can continue for another two to five years.
